newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-IN-FORM STOUTE EYES LONGCHAMP VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IN-FORM STOUTE EYES LONGCHAMP VICTORY.

text.p: Highly successful British trainer Michael Stoute will attempt to carry his winning streak across the Channel to the French 2,000 Guineas on Sunday with fast improving colt Yalaietanee.
Yalaietanee, who beat last year's champion European juvenile Revoque in the Greenham Stakes, heads a three-pronged British assault in the Group One Poule d'Essai des Poulains at Longchamp.
The three-year-old colt grabbed the spotlight in April when he broke Revoque's unbeaten record.
Stoute, regarded as one of the world's premier trainers, produced the winner of last Saturday's 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket in England -- Entrepreneur.
The son of a Barbados ex-police chief has been conquering tracks around the world, chalking up victories in the Breeders' Cup, Japan Cup and the Dubai World Cup.
The forecast for very soft ground will suit Yalaietanee, a mud-runner, down to the ground.
Britain's other entries Bahamian Bounty and Fantastic Fellow have made their mark in France with wins at the Prix Morny and the Prix Djebel respectively.
The Aga Khan's colours, successful last year with Ashkalani, will rely this time on Daylami.
Daylami won the main trial for this race, the Group Three Prix de Fontainebleau, three weeks ago by two lengths.
British-based runners outnumber their Gallic counterparts in the French 1,000 Guineas, the Poule d'Essai des Pouliches, also on Sunday.
Seebe and Red Camellia appear the pick of the fillies.
